newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria has 9.37 bln levs Q2 trade surplus.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria has 9.37 bln levs Q2 trade surplus.

text.p: Bulgaria posted a trade surplus of 9.37 billion levs in the second qarter after a 6.0 billion levs surplus in the first quarter and a 5.44 billion levs surplus in the second quarter of 1995, customs figures show.
BULGARIA MERCHANDISE TRADE, Q2'96 Q1'96 Q2'95
Bulgaria's largest turnover of around 67 billion levs was in trade with countries of the European Union, figures show.
Germany had the largest share in Bulgaria's imports with 11.7 billion levs in the second quarter. The largest importer of Bulgarian goods and services was Italy with 9.8 billion levs.
Bulgaria's exports to the republics of the former Soviet Union totalled 13 billion levs, while imports amounted to 23.8 billion levs.

The year-on-year fall in Bulgaria's exports in the second quarter was mainly due to a decline of state industrial output, which fell a real 4.0 percent year-on-year in the first half of 1996, experts said.
Dollar-denominated foreign trade turnover fell nearly two-fold year-on-year in the second quarter due to the lev's decline against the dollar on the domestic forex market.

The lev, which is now exchanged for more than 230 per dollar, lost around 230 percent of its value since the beginning of 1996 when it traded around 71 to the dollar. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
